report:
I cannot identify a specific objective or domain difference from this evidence.

What I do see:
- The difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at the very first token position (p0) across almost all mid-to-deep layers. That looks like a start-of-sequence/BOS prior shift rather than a task- or domain-specific change.
- The logit-lens at p0 points toward generic sentence-openers and capitalized/proper-noun-y tokens (“Basically”, “Consider”, “TMZ”, “DJI”, etc.), and later toward various sensational/negative words. Across later positions (p1–p4) in deep layers, the direction consistently favors a grab-bag of title-cased nouns and acronyms (“Summary”, “Outcome”, “HDTV”, “Playboy”, “File”, “Computation”, etc.).
- In the deepest layer, a few profane/offensive tokens also appear among the top differences, which could reflect a mild shift in lexical prior or safety tuning, but this is not clean or specific enough to label.

Taken together, this looks like a broad change to the model’s start-of-sequence and general lexical/style priors (possibly BOS handling, casing/proper-noun bias, or safety-tuning intensity), not a clear, interpretable objective or domain (e.g., math, code, translation). Without patchscope continuations, I can’t map it to a concrete behavioral difference.
